doc.title: Chico Hamilton — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Race, family and the younger generation
title: Being the darkest child; his mother taken for a maid
summary: His sister called him blackie, and a sergeant at the train station did not believe the light-skinned woman was his mother; he says he knows who he is.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up under segregation: schools, neighborhoods, Jim Crow

blocks.x: You know, so you’ve just -- you know, what you do -- see at a very early age man, I found out who I was, and personal as a kid, young kid in my family, right. I was the darkest one in my family and my sister used to call me blackie. We never ever, ever used the N word. Never, it was taboo. You never used that word, you know, but the fact that she used to make me feel like inferior -­
You dig? Well man, you know, after it stopped hurting then I realized, that’s her. You know, I’m who I am. I’m what I’m all about. I know me.
Were you actually darker than your father as well?
Yeah? Genetics is something else isn’t it?

Yeah, you dig? They used to think my mother was -- my mother used to carry me in her bucket. They used to think I was the maid’s baby. Man, when I got drafted, leaving to go to San Pedro, my mother came down to the train station to see me off and this sergeant kept going around, Foreststorn Hamilton, Foreststorn Hamilton, and every time he’d pass me I’d say here. He just walked on by. So after about at least a half a dozen times man, he finally -- I said to him, I’m Foreststorn Hamilton and man this dude turned red as a beet. He said, you’re mother wants to see you. He didn’t believe, you know, that was my mother. But anyway, that’s just -­
Have things changed as far as you’re concerned?

I don’t know whether things have changed but I’ve changed. I have no problem with it. If you’ve got a problem with me being what I am, that’s your problem, it’s not mine and if you don’t believe me, if you’re going to mess with me, you’d better come with something because man I’m going to hurt you because I know you only have one intention, that’s to do me bodily harm.
